## The question

> What actually happens when you type a URL and press Enter?

**The walkaway:**

> Find the address, connect, request, receive, render.

## Script

| # | In | Type | s | Narration | Caption text (board) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0:00.0 | hook | 5.9 | You type six words, hit Enter, and a whole website appears. Here's the journey behind that. | Six words, one page |
| 2 | 0:06.9 | explain | 4.8 | First, your browser has to find where that domain actually points. | Find the address |
| 3 | 0:11.7 | analogy | 4.8 | It asks DNS for the right address, like looking up a contact before calling. | Like a phonebook |
| 4 | 0:16.5 | explain | 3.4 | Next, your browser opens a connection to that server. | Connect |
| 5 | 0:19.9 | explain | 5.0 | For a secure site, it also sets up an encrypted HTTPS connection. | Encrypted |
| 6 | 0:24.9 | explain | 3.6 | Then it sends a request: please give me this page. | Ask for the page |
| 7 | 0:28.5 | explain | 7.9 | The server replies with data: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, or links to more files. | Data comes back |
| 8 | 0:35.4 | explain | 3.9 | Your browser reads those pieces and builds the page you see. | It builds the page |
| 9 | 0:39.3 | myth-check | 5.4 | That is why a page can look broken while the server responds fine: one image failed to load. | When it looks broken |
| 10 | 0:45.7 | recap | 4.6 | So the short version: find the address, connect, request, receive, render. | Find, connect, request |
| 11 | 0:49.3 | outro | 4.7 | Next time you type a URL, you'll see the whole journey. | WHERE DOES A URL GO? |
